records.context: **Geometric units depend on the run.** A 2-D run measures in pixels, but a 3-D run measures a volume, and with ``voxel_size_z_um`` / ``voxel_size_xy_um`` set it measures in micrometres — under the *same* column names, because :mod:`spacr.measure` deliberately does not rename ``<object>_area`` (renaming would break every downstream selector). Which one a row is in is recorded on the row itself, in ``measurement_units``. So the unit of a geometric column is a :class:`ConditionalUnit`: :func:`describe_database` reads ``measurement_units`` out of the database it is documenting and resolves it, and a caller who has no database says so and gets the condition spelled out instead of a confident guess. See :data:`MEASUREMENT_UNITS`.
records.label: spacr.feature_dict#3
records.source: **Geometric units depend on the run.** A 2-D run measures in pixels, but a 3-D run measures a volume, and with ``voxel_size_z_um`` / ``voxel_size_xy_um`` set it measures in micrometres — under the *same* column names, because :mod:`spacr.measure` deliberately does not rename ``<object>_area`` (renaming would break every downstream selector). Which one a row is in is recorded on the row itself, in ``measurement_units``. So the unit of a geometric column is a :class:`ConditionalUnit`: :func:`describe_database` reads ``measurement_units`` out of the database it is documenting and resolves it, and a caller who has no database says so and gets the condition spelled out instead of a confident guess. See :data:`MEASUREMENT_UNITS`.
records.translation: **Geometriska enheter beror på körningen.** En 2-D-körning mäter i pixlar, men en 3-D-körning mäter ett volymmått och mäter i mikrometer när ``voxel_size_z_um`` / ``voxel_size_xy_um`` har angetts — under *samma* kolumnnamn, eftersom :mod:`spacr.measure` avsiktligt inte byter namn på ``<object>_area`` (ett namnbyte skulle bryta alla efterföljande väljare). Vilken enhet en rad använder anges på själva raden i ``measurement_units``. Enheten för en geometrisk kolumn är därför en :class:`ConditionalUnit`: :func:`describe_database` läser ``measurement_units`` ur den databas som dokumenteras och bestämmer enheten; en anropare utan databas anger detta och får villkoret uttryckligen beskrivet i stället för en säker gissning. Se :data:`MEASUREMENT_UNITS`.

records.context: **Assumption tests have their own power.** With n = 3, Levene's test has almost no power, so "p = 0.7" means the variances could not be compared, not that they are equal. Using that result to select Student's t can report a difference that is not there. Below :data:`MIN_N_FOR_ASSUMPTIONS` this module records both checks as uninformative, treats the data as not normal, and selects a rank test (Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank when paired, or Kruskal-Wallis for more than two groups). This loses some power when the assumptions hold and avoids false positives when they do not.
records.label: spacr.figures.stats#4
records.source: **Assumption tests have their own power.** With n = 3, Levene's test has almost no power, so "p = 0.7" means the variances could not be compared, not that they are equal. Using that result to select Student's t can report a difference that is not there. Below :data:`MIN_N_FOR_ASSUMPTIONS` this module records both checks as uninformative, treats the data as not normal, and selects a rank test (Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank when paired, or Kruskal-Wallis for more than two groups). This loses some power when the assumptions hold and avoids false positives when they do not.
records.translation: **Test av antaganden har egen statistisk styrka.** Med n = 3 har Levene's test nästan ingen styrka, så "p = 0.7" betyder att varianserna inte kunde jämföras, inte att de är lika. Att använda resultatet för att välja Student's t kan påvisa en skillnad som inte finns. Under :data:`MIN_N_FOR_ASSUMPTIONS` registrerar modulen båda kontrollerna som icke-informativa, behandlar data som icke-normalfördelade och väljer ett rangtest (Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank för parade data eller Kruskal-Wallis för fler än två grupper). Detta minskar styrkan något när antagandena håller och undviker falska positiva när de inte gör det.

records.context: **Selecting on the test split leaks.** :func:`cv_search` scores every trial on cross-validation folds, never on test, and refuses to execute if a caller hands it folds that touch the held-out test indices. It defaults to *grouped* folds (``group_by='well'``) and reuses :func:`spacr.io.make_cv_folds` — extracted image regions from one microplate sample position share focus, illumination and seeding density, so an ungrouped search picks the model that memorised microplate sample positions and reports an inflated score.
records.label: spacr.hyperparam#4
records.source: **Selecting on the test split leaks.** :func:`cv_search` scores every trial on cross-validation folds, never on test, and refuses to run if a caller hands it folds that touch the held-out test indices. It defaults to *grouped* folds (``group_by='well'``) and reuses :func:`spacr.io.make_cv_folds` — crops from one well share focus, illumination and seeding density, so an ungrouped search picks the model that memorised wells and reports an inflated score.
records.translation: **Urval baserat på testdelmängden läcker information.** :func:`cv_search` poängsätter varje försök på korsvalideringsdelmängder, aldrig på testdata, och vägrar köra om anroparen skickar delmängder som omfattar index från den undanhållna testmängden. Som standard används *grupperade* delmängder (``group_by='well'``) och :func:`spacr.io.make_cv_folds` återanvänds — bildutsnitt från samma brunn delar fokus, belysning och såddtäthet, så en ogrupperad sökning väljer modellen som har memorerat brunnar och rapporterar ett uppblåst resultat.

records.context: Image layers are added together, each through its colormap, between its contrast limits, times its opacity; each is drawn by the :data:`VOLUME_RENDERINGS` mode in ``layer.metadata["rendering"]`` (``mip`` when absent). Labels layers are then laid over them in stack order, each object in its :func:`label_color`, by the :data:`LABEL_RENDERINGS` mode (``surface`` when absent) and the layer's opacity. A surface is lit by the :data:`SURFACE_FINISHES` entry in ``layer.metadata["finish"]`` (``matte`` when absent), with normals from the mask itself (:func:`surface_normals`). Hidden layers draw nothing. Every layer must have the volume's shape; image layers draw their first image data channel. :class:`GLVolumeRenderer` draws the same picture on the GPU.

A surface is lit by the :data:`SURFACE_FINISHES` entry in ``layer.metadata["finish"]`` (``matte`` when absent), with normals from the mask itself (:func:`surface_normals`). records.translation: Bildlagren adderas, vart och ett genom sin färgkarta, mellan sina kontrastgränser och multiplicerat med sin opacitet; varje lager ritas med läget från :data:`VOLUME_RENDERINGS` i ``layer.metadata["rendering"]`` (``mip`` om värdet saknas). Etikettlagren läggs sedan ovanpå i stackordning, med varje objekt i sin :func:`label_color`, enligt läget från :data:`LABEL_RENDERINGS` (``surface`` om värdet saknas) och lagrets opacitet. Anything else routes through the same :func:`require_codec` refusal as v2 does. ``.zgroup`` / ``.zarray`` / ``zarr.json`` and the ``zarr_format`` field are read rather than assumed, and an unsupported ``zarr_format`` is refused by number.

records.context: Self-supervised denoising comes before the chain. With ``n2v_denoise`` on, a Noise2Void (N2V2) model per segmentation image data channel is trained by CAREamics, in its own environment, on a sample of the processing session's own raw microscope fields of view -- no clean images are needed -- or read from ``n2v_model``. Each microscope field of view's selected image data channels are denoised after illumination correction and before the PSF and the chain, while the noise is still independent from pixel to pixel, which is what Noise2Void assumes. The checkpoints' hashes and the training record join the same provenance record.
records.label: spacr.psf_pipeline#4
records.source: Self-supervised denoising comes before the chain. With ``n2v_denoise`` on, a Noise2Void (N2V2) model per segmentation channel is trained by CAREamics, in its own environment, on a sample of the run's own raw fields -- no clean images are needed -- or read from ``n2v_model``. Each field's selected channels are denoised after illumination correction and before the PSF and the chain, while the noise is still independent from pixel to pixel, which is what Noise2Void assumes. The checkpoints' hashes and the training record join the same provenance record.
records.translation: Självövervakad brusreducering sker före kedjan. När ``n2v_denoise`` är aktiverat tränar CAREamics, i sin egen miljö, en Noise2Void-modell (N2V2) per segmenteringskanal på ett urval av körningens egna råa bildfält -- inga rena bilder behövs -- eller läser modellen från ``n2v_model``. De valda kanalerna i varje bildfält brusreduceras efter belysningskorrigering och före PSF och kedjan, medan bruset fortfarande är oberoende från pixel till pixel, vilket Noise2Void förutsätter. Kontrollpunkternas hashvärden och träningsposten ingår i samma ursprungspost.

records.context: **The scan never blocks the window.** Walking a plate folder is tens of thousands of ``stat`` calls, and doing it on the main GUI execution path would freeze the application for however long the filesystem takes. Everything goes through :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`, whose completion handlers here are **bound methods** — read that module's docstring for what a closure connected to ``thread.finished`` costs. The background activity spinner follows the processing session registry on its own, so nothing here has to drive it.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.project_browser#5
records.source: **The scan never blocks the window.** Walking a plate folder is tens of thousands of ``stat`` calls, and doing it on the GUI thread would freeze the application for however long the filesystem takes. Everything goes through :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`, whose completion handlers here are **bound methods** — read that module's docstring for what a closure connected to ``thread.finished`` costs. The background activity spinner follows the run registry on its own, so nothing here has to drive it.
records.translation: **Skanningen blockerar aldrig fönstret.** Att gå igenom en plattmapp kräver tiotusentals ``stat``-anrop, och på GUI-tråden skulle detta frysa programmet så länge filsystemet behöver. Allt går genom :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`, vars slutförandehanterare här är **bundna metoder** — läs modulens docstring om kostnaden för en closure ansluten till ``thread.finished``. Indikatorn för bakgrundsaktivitet följer körningsregistret på egen hand, så inget här behöver styra den.

records.context: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable, and the module keeps them separate. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)``, which makes the limits 41% wider and can hide a drift. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#14
records.source: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable, and the module keeps them separate. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)``, which makes the limits 41% wider and can hide a drift. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.translation: De två robusta konstanterna är *inte* utbytbara, och modulen håller dem åtskilda. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) är ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, faktorn som gör MAD för ett normalfördelat stickprov till en väntevärdesriktig skattning av dess SD. En rörlig variationsbredd är ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, absolutbeloppet av en *skillnad* mellan två observationer, så dess skala är ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` och dess median är ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Att multiplicera medianen av en rörlig variationsbredd med 1.4826 överskattar sigma med exakt ``sqrt(2)``, vilket gör gränserna 41% bredare och kan dölja en drift. Båda konstanterna beräknas här från ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` av samma skäl som c4 beräknas från gammafunktionen.

records.context: **Units.** The assay converts pixels per frame into physical units with ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)`` and only when *both* are known; otherwise it reports ``px/frame``. So that a velocity is never read in the wrong unit, the calibration fields start **unset**, every velocity carries its unit, and while the calibration is unknown the panel says so in words instead of silently using the 1.78 px/µm default.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.motility_preview#3
records.source: **Units.** The assay converts pixels per frame into physical units with ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)`` and only when *both* are known; otherwise it reports ``px/frame``. So that a velocity is never read in the wrong unit, the calibration fields start **unset**, every velocity carries its unit, and while the calibration is unknown the panel says so in words instead of silently using the 1.78 px/µm default.
records.translation: **Enheter.** Analysen omvandlar pixlar per bildruta till fysiska enheter med ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)`` och endast när *båda* är kända; annars rapporteras ``px/frame``. För att en hastighet aldrig ska läsas i fel enhet börjar kalibreringsfälten **utan angivna värden**, varje hastighet åtföljs av sin enhet, och så länge kalibreringen är okänd anges detta uttryckligen i panelen i stället för att standardvärdet 1.78 px/µm används i det tysta.

records.context: ``np.load(..., mmap_mode="r")`` is not free: before it maps anything it opens the file and reads the ``.npy`` header, so it is a filesystem round trip on a path the user supplied, and an open costs as much as a stat. Measured on one workstation, one stat under ``/nas_mnt`` -- an ``autofs`` mount whose share was asleep -- had not returned after twenty seconds.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.motility_preview.read_plane_count#1
records.source: ``np.load(..., mmap_mode="r")`` is not free: before it maps anything it opens the file and reads the ``.npy`` header, so it is a filesystem round trip on a path the user supplied, and an open costs as much as a stat. Measured on one workstation, one stat under ``/nas_mnt`` -- an ``autofs`` mount whose share was asleep -- had not returned after twenty seconds.
records.translation: ``np.load(..., mmap_mode="r")`` är inte kostnadsfritt: innan något minnesmappas öppnas filen och dess ``.npy``-huvud läses. Det innebär därför en tur till filsystemet på en sökväg som användaren har angett, och en öppning kostar lika mycket som ett stat-anrop. Vid en mätning på en arbetsstation hade ett stat-anrop under ``/nas_mnt`` -- en ``autofs``-montering vars nätverksresurs var i viloläge -- inte återvänt efter tjugo sekunder.

records.context: So the microplate sample position pass is **not** "the microplate sample position contains many flagged objects". That statistic exists — it is reported as ``flagged_share`` — and it answers a different question: it finds a microplate sample position containing a few *catastrophic* objects (a segmentation blow-up, a piece of dust measured as a cell) while being blind to a uniform shift. The microplate sample position-level robust score finds the uniform shift while being blind to the isolated catastrophe. Both are on the microplate sample position frame because neither subsumes the other.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#29
records.source: So the well pass is **not** "the well contains many flagged objects". That statistic exists — it is reported as ``flagged_share`` — and it answers a different question: it finds a well containing a few *catastrophic* objects (a segmentation blow-up, a piece of dust measured as a cell) while being blind to a uniform shift. The well-level robust score finds the uniform shift while being blind to the isolated catastrophe. Both are on the well frame because neither subsumes the other.
records.translation: Brunnskontrollen betyder alltså **inte** "brunnen innehåller många flaggade objekt". Det måttet finns — det rapporteras som ``flagged_share`` — och besvarar en annan fråga: det hittar en brunn med några få *katastrofala* objekt (en misslyckad segmentering, ett dammkorn mätt som en cell), men upptäcker inte en enhetlig förskjutning. Det robusta måttet på brunnsnivå hittar den enhetliga förskjutningen men upptäcker inte den isolerade katastrofen. Båda finns i brunnstabellen eftersom inget av dem ersätter det andra.

records.context: **One processing-session id, on every log line and every output.** :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per processing session JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, so every log record of the processing session that produced a given file can be retrieved.
records.label: spacr.runctx#2
records.source: **One run id, on every log line and every output.** :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per-run JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, so every log record of the run that produced a given file can be retrieved.
records.translation: **Ett körnings-id på varje loggrad och varje utdataobjekt.** :func:`run_context` skapar ett id, märker varje :class:`logging.LogRecord` som skapas någonstans i processen med det, skriver en JSONL-logg per körning som :func:`read_run_log` läser tillbaka och lämnar *samma* id till :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. En loggrad och ett utdataobjekt kan därför kopplas ihop via ``run_id``, så att alla loggposter från körningen som skapade en viss fil kan hämtas.

records.context: :func:`parse_well` puts an unrecognisable well into *both* slots verbatim, so an unprefixed pair of equal values is that passthrough and not a real row and column. Without this check ``('12', '12')`` looks like row 12 / column 12 and :func:`well_id` renders it ``'L12'`` — a well name for a well that was never identified.

Without this check ``('12', '12')`` looks like row 12 / column 12 and :func:`well_id` renders it ``'L12'`` — a well name for a well that was never identified.
records.translation: :func:`parse_well` lägger en oigenkännlig brunn ordagrant i *båda* positionerna, så ett par lika värden utan prefix är denna vidarebefordran och inte en verklig rad och kolumn. Utan kontrollen ser ``('12', '12')`` ut som rad 12 / kolumn 12 och :func:`well_id` återger det som ``'L12'`` — ett brunnsnamn för en brunn som aldrig identifierades.

records.context: Step 2 of the timeflows plan is a baseline score. Before a third Cellpose head is written, trained and maintained, every frame is segmented independently, the frames are linked by mask overlap, and the result is scored against the ground truth with the standard Cell Tracking Challenge measures. The fork's result is compared with this score; the plan accepts "the plain stitcher is already good enough" as a possible outcome.
records.label: spacr.timeflows_baseline#2
records.source: Step 2 of the timeflows plan is a baseline score. Before a third Cellpose head is written, trained and maintained, every frame is segmented independently, the frames are linked by mask overlap, and the result is scored against the ground truth with the standard Cell Tracking Challenge measures. The fork's result is compared with this score; the plan accepts "the plain stitcher is already good enough" as a possible outcome.
records.translation: Steg 2 i timeflows-planen är ett baslinjeresultat. Innan ett tredje Cellpose-huvud skrivs, tränas och underhålls segmenteras varje bildruta oberoende, bildrutorna länkas via masköverlappning och resultatet jämförs med facit med Cell Tracking Challenge-standardmåtten. Förgreningens resultat jämförs med denna baslinje; planen accepterar "den enkla sammanlänkaren är redan tillräckligt bra" som ett möjligt utfall.

records.context: **Backward compatibility.** A settings CSV written before this exists in every user's project folder, and, as INVARIANTS §6 records, a structured-data name *absent* from the key-value mapping means the workflow falls back to its own default, which can differ from the GUI's, and nothing says so. Every rename here is therefore an alias, not a replacement — :func:`normalize_settings` translates the old name and the old *implicit* basis into the new explicit one, and a processing session from an old CSV does exactly what it did before.
records.label: spacr.training_basis#4
records.source: **Backward compatibility.** A settings CSV written before this exists in every user's project folder, and, as INVARIANTS §6 records, a key *absent* from the dict means the pipeline falls back to its own default, which can differ from the GUI's, and nothing says so. Every rename here is therefore an alias, not a replacement — :func:`normalize_settings` translates the old name and the old *implicit* basis into the new explicit one, and a run from an old CSV does exactly what it did before.
records.translation: **Bakåtkompatibilitet.** En CSV-fil med inställningar skriven innan detta infördes finns i varje användares projektmapp, och enligt INVARIANTS §6 innebär en nyckel som *saknas* i dict att bearbetningskedjan faller tillbaka på sitt eget standardvärde, vilket kan skilja sig från GUI:s utan att detta anges. Varje namnbyte här är därför ett alias, inte en ersättning — :func:`normalize_settings` översätter det gamla namnet och den gamla *underförstådda* basen till den nya uttryckliga, och en körning från en gammal CSV gör exakt det den gjorde tidigare.

records.context: Parameters: df (pd.DataFrame): The input DataFrame. group_col (str): Column name to group by, or a list of column names. Grouping passes ``observed=False``, so unused categories of a Categorical are kept. Rows whose group structured-data name is missing get a ``NaN`` per-row bound, because pandas drops ``NaN`` group structured-data names; they are discarded under 'iqr' and kept under 'zscore'. value_col (str): Column containing values to check for outliers. A name that is not in the frame raises ``KeyError``. method (str): 'iqr' or 'zscore'. Anything else raises ``ValueError``. The two agree on tiny groups: a one-row group has an undefined standard deviation, and since one row cannot be an outlier within its own group it is KEPT under both. threshold (float): Multiplier on the IQR (default 1.5), or the z-score cutoff. Must be >= 0; a negative value inverts the keep-band and raises ``ValueError``, because under 'iqr' it would empty every group with a nonzero IQR. ``0`` under 'zscore' keeps only rows sitting exactly on the group mean. Under 'zscore' an outlier inflates its own group's standard deviation, so the usual cutoffs keep more rows than 'iqr' does on the same data.
records.label: spacr.utils.remove_outliers_by_group#2
records.source: Parameters: df (pd.DataFrame): The input DataFrame. group_col (str): Column name to group by, or a list of column names. Grouping passes ``observed=False``, so unused categories of a Categorical are kept. Rows whose group key is missing get a ``NaN`` per-row bound, because pandas drops ``NaN`` group keys; they are discarded under 'iqr' and kept under 'zscore'. value_col (str): Column containing values to check for outliers. A name that is not in the frame raises ``KeyError``. method (str): 'iqr' or 'zscore'. Anything else raises ``ValueError``. The two agree on tiny groups: a one-row group has an undefined standard deviation, and since one row cannot be an outlier within its own group it is KEPT under both. threshold (float): Multiplier on the IQR (default 1.5), or the z-score cutoff. Must be >= 0; a negative value inverts the keep-band and raises ``ValueError``, because under 'iqr' it would empty every group with a nonzero IQR. ``0`` under 'zscore' keeps only rows sitting exactly on the group mean. Under 'zscore' an outlier inflates its own group's standard deviation, so the usual cutoffs keep more rows than 'iqr' does on the same data.
records.translation: Parametrar: df (pd.DataFrame): Indata som DataFrame. group_col (str): Kolumnnamnet att gruppera efter, eller en lista med kolumnnamn. Grupperingen skickar ``observed=False``, så oanvända kategorier i en Categorical behålls. Rader vars gruppnyckel saknas får en radvis gräns på ``NaN``, eftersom pandas tar bort gruppnycklar med ``NaN``; de tas bort med 'iqr' och behålls med 'zscore'. value_col (str): Kolumnen med värden som ska kontrolleras för avvikare. Ett namn som inte finns i tabellen ger ``KeyError``. method (str): 'iqr' eller 'zscore'. Allt annat ger ``ValueError``. De två metoderna är överens om mycket små grupper: en grupp med en rad har en odefinierad standardavvikelse, och eftersom en rad inte kan vara en avvikare i sin egen grupp BEHÅLLS den med båda. threshold (float): Multiplikator för IQR (standard 1.5), eller gränsen för z-poäng. Måste vara >= 0; ett negativt värde vänder på intervallet som behålls och ger ``ValueError``, eftersom det med 'iqr' skulle tömma varje grupp vars IQR inte är noll. ``0`` med 'zscore' behåller endast rader som ligger exakt på gruppens medelvärde. Med 'zscore' höjer en avvikare sin egen grupps standardavvikelse, så de vanliga gränserna behåller fler rader än 'iqr' på samma data.

records.context: **All or nothing.** SQLite's DDL *is* transactional, but Python's sqlite3 driver only opens an implicit transaction for DML (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ REPLACE) — an ``ALTER TABLE`` runs in autocommit and lands immediately. The transaction is therefore opened explicitly and rolled back on any error, so a call that raises applies no rename, and the connection is closed in a ``finally``.
records.label: spacr.utils.rename_columns_in_db#4
records.source: **All or nothing.** SQLite's DDL *is* transactional, but Python's sqlite3 driver only opens an implicit transaction for DML (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ REPLACE) — an ``ALTER TABLE`` runs in autocommit and lands immediately. The transaction is therefore opened explicitly and rolled back on any error, so a call that raises applies no rename, and the connection is closed in a ``finally``.
records.translation: **Allt eller inget.** DDL i SQLite *är* transaktionellt, men drivrutinen sqlite3 i Python öppnar bara en implicit transaktion för DML (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ REPLACE) — ett ``ALTER TABLE`` körs med autocommit och får omedelbar effekt. Transaktionen öppnas därför uttryckligen och återställs vid varje fel, så ett anrop som ger ett undantag inte genomför något namnbyte, och anslutningen stängs i ett ``finally``.
